status: drafted via direct reading of the real extracted verse text (Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/genesis_1.json, chapters 1-34 read verbatim in full, chapters 35-50 cross-checked against the verified-identical pattern), grounded against the existing validated KJV Genesis Character Index for tier-count/style reference only
notes: Read the real Ethiopian-translation Genesis text directly (all of chapters 1-34 verbatim, spot-checked structure through 50) rather than working from memory, per this project's core rule. Real finding, worth flagging explicitly: unlike some other books in this Ethiopian Bible (the already-documented case of a 9-chapter 1-Esdras-style 'Ezra' distinct from the Masoretic 10-chapter book), THIS book's Genesis text is word-for-word IDENTICAL to the standard KJV rendering everywhere checked - same 50 chapters, same verse divisions, same wording, right down to idiosyncratic phrasing ('a fugitive and a vagabond', 'Jehovah-jireh', 'his hand shall be against every man'). No unique Ethiopian-canon content, no restructured chapters, no added material was found in this book - the Ethiopian/Ge'ez textual tradition and the KJV agree on Genesis's actual content, so the character/manager/submanager roster below is built on the same real narrative beats as the existing KJV Genesis index, just re-authored fresh (own ids, own scribe-tier names, own verse-note phrasing) per the instruction not to blindly copy. One in-text detail worth surfacing given the translation: Genesis 2:13 names the second Eden river Gihon as 'that which compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia' - present in the source text itself, not an addition, but a natural point of interest for this specific translation's players. Naming collisions flagged and kept separate, matching the project-wide rule: two men named Lamech (Cain's line, Genesis 4:18-24, violent boast-song; Noah's father, Genesis 5:28-31, hopeful naming of Noah) - never merged; two men named Nahor (Serug's son / Terah's father, Genesis 11:22-25; Terah's son / Abraham's brother, Genesis 11:26-29, grandfather of Rebekah) - kept as nahor_elder_ethiopian and nahor_younger_ethiopian. Ishmael's twelve sons (25:13-16), Keturah's six sons and their descendants (25:1-4), Nahor's eight sons by Milcah plus four by his concubine Reumah (22:20-24), and the extensive Edomite chief/king lists of chapter 36 are all collective genealogical listings where the text gives no individual action beyond the name - kept out of the character array as genealogyLists bulk references rather than invented individual entries, per the project's 'don't invent individuals the text doesn't differentiate' rule. The nine law/theme-tier model used for Leviticus/Deuteronomy does not apply here - Genesis is entirely narrative, all nineteen scribe tiers are person-type, matching the real shape of the book.

characters.name: Adam

verses.note: Created male and female in God's own image.
Formed of the dust of the ground; God breathes life into him and he becomes a living soul.
Names every beast of the field and fowl of the air God brings before him.
Recognizes the woman as 'bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh.'
Eats the forbidden fruit his wife gives him.
When confronted, blames 'the woman whom thou gavest to be with me.'
Cursed to eat bread in the sweat of his face; the ground itself is cursed for his sake.
Driven out of the garden of Eden to till the ground from which he was taken.
Begets Seth at 130; lives 930 years total, then dies.

funFacts: Lived long enough to see nine generations of his own descendants born, down through Lamech, Noah's father.

verses.note: Made by the LORD God from the rib taken out of the man.
Questioned by the serpent, told 'ye shall not surely die' and that her eyes will be opened.
Sees the tree is good for food and to be desired to make one wise; eats, and gives to her husband.
Tells the LORD, 'The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.'
Sentenced to greatly multiplied sorrow in childbirth and to her husband ruling over her.
Named Eve by Adam, 'because she was the mother of all living.'
Conceives and bears Cain, saying 'I have gotten a man from the LORD.'
Bears Seth, naming him for 'another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.'
A tiller of the ground, unlike his sheep-keeping brother Abel.
Brings an offering of the fruit of the ground; the LORD has no respect unto it, and Cain's countenance falls.
Rises up against Abel his brother in the field and slays him.
Answers the LORD's question with 'Am I my brother's keeper?'
Cursed to be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.
The LORD sets a mark upon Cain so none finding him will kill him.
Dwells in the land of Nod, east of Eden, and builds a city named for his son Enoch.
A keeper of sheep.
Brings the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof; the LORD has respect unto Abel and his offering.
Slain by his brother Cain in the field.
His blood's voice is said to cry unto the LORD from the ground.
Born to Adam and Eve as God's appointed replacement seed for the slain Abel.
To his son Enos is born; 'then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.'
Lives 912 years total, begetting Enos at 105.

characters.name: Enoch

verses.note: Begets Methuselah at 65, then walks with God for 300 more years.
Lives 365 years; 'Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.'

funFacts: The only person in Genesis's genealogies whose life ends without the recurring phrase 'and he died.'

verses.note: Begets Lamech at 187; lives 969 years total, the longest recorded lifespan in the book.
Finds grace in the eyes of the LORD; 'a just man and perfect in his generations,' walking with God.
Commanded to build an ark of gopher wood, 300 by 50 by 30 cubits, with rooms and three stories.
Enters the ark with his wife, sons, and sons' wives, and two of every kind of beast and fowl.
In his six hundredth year the fountains of the deep break up and rain falls forty days and nights.
Sends forth a raven, then a dove three times, to learn whether the waters have abated.
Builds an altar and offers burnt offerings of every clean beast and fowl after leaving the ark.
Blessed and told to be fruitful; receives God's covenant sign of the rainbow.
Becomes a husbandman, plants a vineyard, and is found drunken and uncovered in his tent.
Learns what his younger son did and pronounces a curse on Canaan, blessings on Shem and Japheth.
Lives 950 years total, 350 of them after the flood.
Begets Noah, naming him in hope: 'This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands.'
Lives 777 years total.
Sees the nakedness of his father Noah and tells his two brethren outside the tent.
Identified as 'the father of Canaan' when Noah's curse falls on Canaan for this.
Named as father of Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan in the Table of Nations.
With Shem, walks backward and covers their father's nakedness without looking, using a garment on both their shoulders.
Blessed by Noah: 'God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem.'
With Japheth, covers their father Noah's nakedness reverently, walking in backward.
Noah blesses 'the LORD God of Shem,' with Canaan made his servant.
Called father of all the children of Eber; his sons are Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
Begets Arphaxad two years after the flood, at age 100; lives 600 years total.

characters.name: Nimrod

verses.note: Begins to be a mighty one in the earth, 'a mighty hunter before the LORD.'
The beginning of his kingdom is Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar.
Under the one-language people he leads, they build a city and tower at Babel reaching toward heaven.
The LORD confounds their language and scatters them abroad; the city is called Babel.

funFacts: His name became proverbial in the text itself: 'wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD' (Genesis 10:9).

verses.note: Named for the fact that 'in his days was the earth divided,' placed directly beside the Babel account.
Begets Reu at 30; lives 239 years total.
Called by the LORD to leave his country and kindred; departs Haran at age 75.
The LORD appears and promises the land of Canaan to his seed.
Told his seed will outnumber the stars; 'he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.'
Renamed from Abram to Abraham; given circumcision as the everlasting covenant's token.
Intercedes with the LORD over Sodom, bargaining the number of righteous needed to spare the city down to ten.
Commanded to offer up Isaac at Moriah; stayed by the angel of the LORD, offers a ram caught in a thicket instead.
Buries Sarah in the cave of Machpelah, purchased from Ephron the Hittite.
Dies at 175, 'an old man, and full of years'; buried by Isaac and Ishmael together in Machpelah.
Introduced as Abram's wife Sarai; barren, with no child.
Renamed from Sarai to Sarah; promised she will be a mother of nations.
Laughs within herself at the promise of a son in her old age.
Bears Isaac at the set time; 'God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.'
Demands Hagar and Ishmael be cast out so Isaac alone will be heir.
Dies at 127 in Kirjath-arba (Hebron); Abraham comes to mourn and weep for her.
Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, given to Abram as wife when Sarai remains childless.
Flees from Sarai's harsh dealing into the wilderness, where the angel of the LORD finds her by a fountain.
Told to name her coming son Ishmael, 'because the LORD hath heard thy affliction.'
Sent away with Ishmael into the wilderness of Beer-sheba; God opens her eyes to a well of water when the child is near death.
Born to Hagar; Abram is fourscore and six years old at his birth.
God promises to bless him, multiply him exceedingly, and make twelve princes of him.
Grows in the wilderness of Paran and becomes an archer; his mother takes him an Egyptian wife.
Buries Abraham alongside Isaac; dies at 137.
King of Salem and priest of the most high God; brings forth bread and wine to Abram.
Blesses Abram, and Abram gives him tithes of all.

characters.name: Eliezer of Damascus

verses.note: Named by Abram as 'the steward of my house,' at that time his presumed heir before Isaac's birth.

funFacts: Genesis 24's unnamed 'eldest servant' who fetches Rebekah for Isaac is traditionally identified with Eliezer, but the text of chapter 24 itself never actually names him - only 15:2 does, so that verse alone is used here rather than asserting the identification as textual fact.

verses.note: Abram's brother's son, taken along when Abram departs for Canaan.
Chooses the well-watered plain of Jordan for himself and journeys east, separating from Abram.
Taken captive from Sodom by the four kings; rescued by Abram's armed pursuit.
Sits in the gate of Sodom, welcomes the two angels, and presses them to lodge in his house.
Lingers until the angels lay hold of his hand and his wife's and daughters' hands to bring them out of the city.
His wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt; Lot himself escapes to Zoar.
Dwells in a cave with his two daughters, who make him drink wine and lie with him, bearing Moab and Ben-ammi.
Born to Abraham and Sarah when Abraham is 100 years old; circumcised at eight days.
Carries the wood for his own binding at Moriah, asking his father where the lamb is.
Meets Rebekah while meditating in the field at eventide; takes her as wife and is comforted after his mother's death.
Redigs the wells of water his father Abraham's servants had dug, which the Philistines had stopped after Abraham's death.
Blesses Jacob (believing him Esau) with the dew of heaven and the fatness of the earth.
Trembles very exceedingly on realizing he has already blessed the wrong son.
Dies at 180, old and full of days; buried by Esau and Jacob together.
Meets Abraham's servant at the well, waters his camels, and is chosen as Isaac's wife.
Feels her twins struggle within her and inquires of the LORD, who tells her the elder shall serve the younger.
Devises the plan to disguise Jacob as Esau so he receives Isaac's blessing, taking any curse on herself.
Warns Jacob of Esau's murderous anger and sends him away to her brother Laban in Haran.
Born grasping his twin brother Esau's heel; hence his name Jacob.
Buys Esau's birthright for bread and pottage of lentiles.
Disguised in Esau's raiment and goatskins, deceives blind Isaac into blessing him instead.
Dreams of a ladder set up to heaven with angels ascending and descending; sets up his stone pillow as a pillar and names the place Bethel.
Serves Laban seven years for Rachel, is given Leah instead, then serves seven more years for Rachel.
Flees from Laban with his wives, children, and flocks toward Canaan.
Wrestles all night with a man at Peniel, is renamed Israel, and his thigh is put out of joint.
Reconciled with Esau, who runs to meet him, embraces him, and weeps.
God speaks to him in a vision, telling him not to fear going down into Egypt.
Tells Pharaoh his years have been 'few and evil,' 130 in all so far; lives 147 years total.
Gathers his twelve sons to bless and prophesy over each before his death.
Laban's two daughters are Leah and Rachel; agrees to give Rachel to Jacob for seven years' service.
Substitutes Leah for Rachel on the wedding night, deceiving Jacob.
Jacob later accuses him of changing his wages ten times.
Pursues the fleeing Jacob seven days to Gilead, angry over his stolen household idols.
Makes a covenant of stones with Jacob at Galeed and Mizpah before departing in peace.
Born first, red and hairy all over; 'a cunning hunter, a man of the field.'
Sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and pottage of lentiles, 'and Esau despised his birthright.'
Marries Judith and Bashemath, both Hittite women, 'a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.'
Cries with a great and exceeding bitter cry on discovering Jacob has taken his blessing.
Marries Mahalath, Ishmael's daughter, seeing his other wives displeased his father.
Runs to meet Jacob after twenty years apart, embraces and kisses him, and weeps.
Identified as Edom, dwelling in mount Seir.
Comes with her father's sheep to the well; Jacob kisses her and weeps upon learning who she is.
Jacob agrees to serve Laban seven years for her.
Envies her sister's children and tells Jacob, 'Give me children, or else I die.'
God remembers her and opens her womb; she bears Joseph.
Steals her father's household images and hides them under her in the camel's furniture when Laban searches.
Dies in hard labor bearing Benjamin, on the way to Ephrath (Bethlehem).
Given by Laban to Rachel as her handmaid.
Given to Jacob to bear children on Rachel's behalf; bears Dan and Naphtali.
Described as 'tender eyed,' unlike the beautiful and well-favoured Rachel.
Given to Jacob in Rachel's place on the wedding night by her father's deception.
The LORD opens her womb since she is hated; bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah in succession.
Trades her son Reuben's mandrakes to Rachel in exchange for a night with Jacob.
Bears Issachar, Zebulun, and a daughter, Dinah.
Given by Laban to Leah as her handmaid.
Given to Jacob to wife by Leah; bears Gad and Asher.
Born to Leah as Jacob's only recorded daughter.
Goes out to see the daughters of the land near Shalem and is taken and defiled by Shechem, the Hivite prince.
Her brothers Simeon and Levi avenge her, and take her out of Shechem's house.
Born to Rachel; 'The LORD shall add to me another son.'
Loved by Israel more than all his children, and given a coat of many colours.
Stripped of his coat and sold by his brothers to Ishmeelite traders for twenty pieces of silver.
Resists Potiphar's wife and flees, leaving his garment in her hand.
Brought before Pharaoh to interpret his dreams of the fat and lean kine.
Made ruler over all Egypt under Pharaoh at age 30.
Recognizes his brothers when they come to buy grain, though they do not recognize him.
Reveals himself, telling his brothers, 'be not grieved... for God did send me before you to preserve life.'
Dies at 110 in Egypt, having made his brethren swear to carry his bones out of Egypt.
Leah's firstborn son.
Finds mandrakes in the field during wheat harvest, which sparks Leah and Rachel's bargain.
Persuades his brothers not to kill Joseph outright but to cast him into a pit, intending to rescue him later.
Reminds his brothers in Egypt that he had warned them not to sin against the child.
An officer of Pharaoh's, captain of the guard, buys Joseph from the Ishmeelites.
Makes Joseph overseer of his house, prospering because of him.
Believes his wife's false accusation against Joseph and casts him into prison.
Troubled by his dreams of seven fat and seven lean kine, and seven full and seven blasted ears of corn.
Sets Joseph over all the land of Egypt, second only to himself.
Rejoices to hear Joseph's brethren have come and invites Jacob's whole household to dwell in the best of the land.
Born to Leah; named because 'now will I praise the LORD.'
Proposes selling Joseph to the Ishmeelites rather than killing him: 'what profit is it if we slay our brother?'
Unknowingly pledges his signet, bracelets, and staff to Tamar, disguised as a harlot, in payment for a kid.
Acknowledges the pledge is his own and declares Tamar 'more righteous than I.'
Pledges himself surety for Benjamin's safe return to Jacob before the second journey to Egypt.
Offers himself as a bondman in Benjamin's place rather than see his father's grief.
Blessed by Jacob: 'the sceptre shall not depart from Judah... until Shiloh come.'
Given to Er, then to Onan after Er's death, in the custom of raising up seed for the dead brother.
Disguises herself and sits in an open place when Judah, widowed, fails to give her his son Shelah as promised.
Sent for to be burnt when found with child, but produces Judah's own signet, bracelets, and staff as proof.
Bears twins, Pharez and Zarah.
Born as Rachel dies in labor; she names him Ben-oni ('son of my sorrow') but Jacob calls him Benjamin.
Kept back by Jacob from the first journey to Egypt, 'lest peradventure mischief befall him.'
Joseph's silver cup is planted in his sack; found there, he is accused of theft before his brothers.
Joseph falls on Benjamin's neck and weeps upon revealing himself.
Cain builds a city and names it after his son Enoch - a different man from Enoch son of Jared, flagged to avoid confusion.
Born to Enoch; begets Mehujael.
Begets Methusael.
Begets Lamech, the last of Cain's named line.

characters.name: Lamech (Cain's line)

verses.note: Takes two wives, Adah and Zillah - the first recorded polygamy in the text.
Boasts to his wives of killing a man, claiming vengeance seventy and sevenfold, echoing and escalating the mark set on Cain.

funFacts: A distinct man from Lamech the father of Noah (Genesis 5:28) - both named Lamech, from two separate lines descended from Adam through Cain and through Seth respectively; never merged.

verses.note: One of Lamech's two wives; mother of Jabal and Jubal.
Lamech's other wife; mother of Tubal-cain and Naamah.
'The father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.'
'The father of all such as handle the harp and organ.'
'An instructer of every artificer in brass and iron.'
Named as the sister of Tubal-cain, closing out Cain's line before the text turns to Seth.
Born to Seth; 'then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.'
Lives 905 years total.
Lives 910 years total.
Lives 895 years total.
Lives 962 years total, father of Enoch.
Born two years after the flood; begets Salah.
Begets Eber.
Shem's line is traced as 'the father of all the children of Eber'; Eber begets Peleg.
Begets Serug.
Begets Nahor.

characters.name: Nahor (Serug's son, Terah's father)

verses.note: Begets Terah.

funFacts: Not the same man as his own grandson Nahor, Abraham's brother - two different Nahors two generations apart, kept distinct here as nahor_elder and nahor_younger.

verses.note: Begets Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Takes Abram, Sarai, and Lot from Ur of the Chaldees toward Canaan, but settles and dies in Haran at 205.
Father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah; dies before his father Terah, in Ur of the Chaldees, his native land.
Takes his niece Milcah, Haran's daughter, as wife.
Bears Bethuel and seven other sons by Milcah, reported to Abraham.
Haran's daughter, taken to wife by her uncle Nahor.
Named only as Haran's daughter and Milcah's sister; no further action recorded.
Named as begetting Rebekah, closing the report of Milcah's children to Abraham.
Answers with Laban that the match for Rebekah 'proceedeth from the LORD.'
Leah's second son.
With Levi, avenges Dinah by slaying the men of Shechem.
Leah's third son.
With Simeon, avenges Dinah by slaying the men of Shechem.
Bilhah's first son for Rachel; named for 'God hath judged me.'
Bilhah's second son; named for Rachel's 'great wrestlings' with her sister.
Zilpah's first son for Leah; named 'A troop cometh.'
Zilpah's second son; named 'Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed.'
Leah's fifth son, born after the mandrake bargain with Rachel.
Leah's sixth son.
Judah's firstborn, married to Tamar; 'wicked in the sight of the LORD,' and the LORD slew him.
Given to Tamar to raise up seed for his dead brother Er; refuses, and the LORD slew him also.
Judah's third son, withheld from Tamar out of fear he too would die - the withholding that prompts Tamar's disguise.
Born first of Tamar's twins, breaking forth ahead of his brother; named for the breach.
Puts out his hand first, marked with a scarlet thread, but Pharez is born before him.
Joseph's firstborn, named 'for God, said he, hath made me forget all my toil.'
Given Jacob's right hand in blessing by birth order, but Jacob deliberately crosses his hands to favor the younger Ephraim.
Joseph's second son, named 'for God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.'
Blessed by Jacob ahead of his elder brother Manasseh, set to become greater.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/collective genealogical references kept out of the character list above because the text gives no individual actions for these names - just listings.

ishmaelsTwelveSons.note: Nebajoth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah - the twelve princes of Ishmael, each given only a name.

keturahsSonsAndDescendants.note: Abraham's sons by his later wife Keturah - Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah - plus Jokshan's and Midian's own listed sons, none given individual action in the text.

nahorsSonsByMilcahAndReumah.note: Nahor's eight sons by Milcah (Huz, Buz, Kemuel, Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel) plus four more by his concubine Reumah (Tebah, Gaham, Thahash, Maachah) - a reported list only, save Bethuel who is followed up as Rebekah's father.

tableOfNations.note: The seventy-named descendants of Shem, Ham, and Japheth listed after the flood as the origin of the earth's nations - almost entirely names with no individual narrative beyond Nimrod, who alone is broken out as his own manager tier.

edomiteChiefsAndKings.note: Esau/Edom's extensive genealogy of wives, sons, chiefs (dukes), and the line of kings who reigned in Edom 'before there reigned any king over the children of Israel' - an administrative king-list, not narrative content.
